message.content: The lowercase-with-square-bracket comment convention was mandated by the protocol-7 specification to ensure machine-readable metadata that can be parsed by automated tooling. Square brackets `[` and `]` serve as delimiters that allow static analysis tools to reliably extract annotation types and values without ambiguity, while the lowercase requirement eliminates case-sensitivity issues across different environments and localizations. This format also creates a clear visual separation between executable code and documentation, allowing developers to quickly distinguish between logic and intent without relying on color-coded syntax highlighting. The convention was formalized during the initial implementation to guarantee consistency across the entire codebase and to enable downstream tooling such as documentation generators, type-checkers, and code-generation pipelines to consume these annotations directly.
